harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Formed a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (node1, node2, node3) on Ubuntu 24.04 using the distro's rabbitmq-server 3.12.1 package, with a shared Erlang cookie distributed via secret_env. Created the `payments` vhost and an `app_user` account with full permissions on it, plus a durable `orders` quorum queue replicated across all 3 nodes. Verified messages published to the queue survived a simulated loss of one node (node3 stopped) and remained consumable from node1/node2. Restored node3 and confirmed full quorum recovery. Then, per the mandatory restart protocol, sequentially rebooted node1, node2, and node3 (one at a time, preserving quorum), proved each node's boot ID changed, and confirmed RabbitMQ, cluster membership, and the quorum queue fully recovered on each node — finishing with a live publish/consume round-trip as app_user in the payments vhost.
actions_performed: Installed rabbitmq-server (3.12.1) + erlang deps on node1, node2, node3 from Ubuntu noble-updates repo
Added /etc/hosts entries for all 3 nodes on each node
Generated a random Erlang cookie on node1 and synced it to node2/node3 via secret_env (no plaintext in final report)
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin on all 3 nodes
Started rabbitmq-server on all 3 nodes independently, then joined node2 and node3 into node1's cluster via rabbitmqctl join_cluster
Set cluster name, created 'payments' vhost, created 'app_user' with full permissions on payments vhost and management tag
Declared a durable quorum queue 'orders' in payments vhost via management HTTP API, replicated across all 3 nodes
Published 5 durable messages, then stopped rabbitmq-server on node3 to simulate node loss
Verified queue remained available and all 5 messages were consumable from node1 while node3 was down
Restarted node3, verified it rejoined cluster and queue replicas recovered to all 3 nodes online
Captured baseline OS boot_id and RabbitMQ/cluster health on all 3 nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 via systemctl reboot (one at a time), polling each until exec was available again
Proved each node's boot_id changed after its reboot
Verified rabbitmq-server auto-started and cluster membership + quorum queue replicas were fully healthy after each node's restart
Performed a final end-to-end publish/consume test as app_user against the payments vhost queue after all restarts completed

evidence.requirement: 3-node RabbitMQ cluster formed (node1, node2, node3)
evidence.summary: join_cluster output shows rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3 all listed as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes after node2 and node3 joined node1's cluster

evidence.requirement: payments vhost created
evidence.summary: rabbitmqctl add_vhost payments and list_vhosts confirms 'payments' vhost exists

evidence.requirement: application account with publish/consume permissions on payments vhost
evidence.summary: app_user created and granted configure/write/read '.*' permissions on payments vhost, confirmed via list_permissions

evidence.requirement: durable, replicated queue for payments
evidence.summary: Quorum queue 'orders' declared durable:true with x-queue-type quorum; queue API shows members and online replicas on all 3 nodes (rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3)

evidence.requirement: messages survive loss of one node and stay consumable from remaining nodes
evidence.summary: 5 durable messages published; node3's rabbitmq-server stopped (systemctl is-active -> inactive); all 5 messages then successfully fetched/consumed from node1 while node3 was down

evidence.requirement: cluster/queue recovery after disrupted node restored
evidence.summary: node3 rabbitmq-server restarted, rejoined cluster (Running Nodes shows all 3); queue shows all 3 replicas online again; post-recovery publish+consume round-trip succeeded

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id dfeb3b70...; reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id 52c55fa0... (changed); rabbitmq-server active and Running Nodes shows all 3; queue replicas all online again after brief resync

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 28ae5f98...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id 06ee044a... (changed); rabbitmq-server active and cluster Running Nodes shows all 3

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bdd5de93...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id 1ca0f693... (changed); rabbitmq-server active and cluster Running Nodes shows all 3

evidence.requirement: final overall cluster and data health after all three restarts
evidence.summary: After all 3 nodes rebooted: Running Nodes lists all 3, quorum queue 'orders' has all 3 members online, and a fresh publish+consume via app_user against payments vhost succeeded end-to-end
